sections.overview: This noctuid moth ranges from the Iberian Peninsula eastward to Siberia.
sections.identification: UKMoths gives a wingspan of 32–45 mm and notes its grassland association; adult size alone does not separate it from T. cespitis.
sections.habitat: In Britain it uses rough grassland and downland.
sections.diet: Its larvae feed on grasses, including fescues.
sections.behavior: Adults fly mainly in August and September, and males are often attracted to lights.
sections.reproduction: The caterpillar overwinters, then feeds on grasses before pupating; species accounts give no detailed courtship description.
sections.ecology: Like T. cespitis, it is grass-feeding; its caterpillars become brown and develop earlier after winter, so see that profile for the contrast.
sections.conservation: The German species account describes T. decimalis as not threatened; local distribution can still vary by region.
